summary: Tennis 48-hour lookahead window verified end-to-end. Backend: 5/5 pytest cases pass (test_tennis_48h_window.py). /api/version returns data_version='2026.06.22-tennis-48h-window'. /api/picks/today?sport=Tennis returns 8 picks all dated 2026-06-23 (tomorrow) — today's matches have already started and are filtered out by the serializer, which is expected per the agent context note. /api/picks/today (no filter) shows Tennis tomorrow picks alongside MLB. Direct call to fetch_extra_tennis_picks(days_ahead=1) returns picks for BOTH 2026-06-22 and 2026-06-23. MLB pitcher H2H endpoint for pick 48600ae0-0268-5e82-99f2-8aab24d563cd still returns 200 (no regression). Frontend: logged in as demo@lockscore.ai, selected Tennis filter chip — UI displays 'TOMORROW · 8 GAMES' section with the EXTENDED badge and all four target players (Tsitsipas, Humbert, Borges, Fearnley) plus Tabilo, Brooksby, Arnaldi, Fery. All tier markers show ATP 250 (Mallorca/Eastbourne). Two non-blocking observations: (1) lock_score values surface ≥91 even though tennis_extra/picks.py caps base lock at _MAX_LOCK=90 — looks like the self-heal validator (fixed_lock=168) bumps them post-write; main agent may want to confirm whether scraped picks should bypass the lock-score uplift. (2) edge_percent shows +2.0..+2.4% in the UI rather than the 0.0 written by the picks generator, again attributable to the validator's edge fix-up (fixed_edge=181) — does not block surfacing on the tennis_ml_q $or branch.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py line 837: `p['id'] = str(uuid.uuid5(namespace, ext)) if ext else str(uuid.uuid4())` — tennis_extra picks have no `external_id`, so their carefully built deterministic `pid` (sha1 of player+tournament+event_date) gets replaced by uuid4() each refresh. This means scraped picks lose stability across refresh cycles (each refresh creates a brand-new pick id even for the same match). Consider hashing `pid` into the namespace UUID when source=='tennis_extra' so the docstring guarantee 'pick id hash uses the match's *event_date* so today's Smith vs Jones and tomorrow's Smith vs Jones never collide' actually holds post-write.
tennis_extra/scraper.py _resolve_commence_time hard-codes CEST (UTC+2). After Oct 26 2026 (CET = UTC+1) all commence_time values will be 1 hour ahead. Not blocking now but worth a TODO.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing demo@lockscore.ai user and live scraped data from TennisExplorer (cached).
